record.original_question: For physically structured random measurement matrices built from Fourier transforms and random phase diffusers, such as A = F D F and A = F D_1 F D_2 ... F D_l, can one prove information-theoretic and algorithmic bounds for the weak-recovery threshold alpha_WR and the full-recovery threshold alpha_FR?

evidence.quote: Question 6.5. Can we derive (information theory and algorithmic) bounds on the threshold values αWR and αFR for the measurement matrices of the form A = FDF and A = FD1FD2 · · · FDℓ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the phase retrieval problem in the high-dimensional asymptotic regime: a hidden signal $x^\star \in \mathbb{C}^n$ (drawn, say, uniformly from the complex sphere of radius $\sqrt{n}$) is observed through magnitude-only measurements
$$y = |A x^\star|^2 \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^m,$$
where $A \in \mathbb{C}^{m\times n}$ is a measurement matrix, $m = \alpha n$, and $\alpha>0$ is the oversampling ratio. The squared magnitude is taken entrywise.

For a sequence of estimators $\hat{x}=\hat{x}(y,A)$, define the (normalized) overlap
$$q(\hat{x},x^\star) = \frac{|\langle \hat{x}, x^\star\rangle|}{\|\hat{x}\|\,\|x^\star\|}.$$
The information-theoretic weak-recovery threshold is
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{WR}} = \inf\{\alpha>0 : \exists\,\hat{x}\text{ with }\liminf_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\,q(\hat{x},x^\star)^2 > 0\},$$
and the full-recovery threshold is
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{FR}} = \inf\{\alpha>0 : \exists\,\hat{x}\text{ with }\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\,q(\hat{x},x^\star)^2 = 1\}.$$
Algorithmic counterparts $\alpha_{\mathrm{WR}}^{\mathrm{alg}}$ and $\alpha_{\mathrm{FR}}^{\mathrm{alg}}$ are defined analogously, restricting to polynomial-time estimators.

Now restrict the ensemble of measurement matrices to the physically structured "Fourier–diffuser" families:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $A = F D F$, where $F$ is the (unitary) discrete Fourier transform on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and $D = \mathrm{diag}(d_1,\dots,d_n)$ with $d_i$ i.i.d.\ uniform on the unit circle in $\mathbb{C}$;
\item[(ii)] More generally, $A = F D_1 F D_2 \cdots F D_\ell$ for a fixed integer $\ell\geq 2$, where each $D_k$ is an independent diagonal matrix of i.i.d.\ uniform unit-modulus phases.
\end{itemize}
(For $m<n$, the construction is followed by sub-sampling $m$ rows; for $m>n$, by independent repetitions.)

Problem: Establish information-theoretic and algorithmic bounds (ideally, sharp values) for the weak-recovery threshold $\alpha_{\mathrm{WR}}$ and the full-recovery threshold $\alpha_{\mathrm{FR}}$ for the phase retrieval problem with measurement matrices drawn from the ensembles (i) and (ii).
artifact.category_tag: Phase retrieval thresholds for structured random matrices
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (2024–2025) study structured random phase retrieval with cascaded Fourier–diffuser matrices and demonstrate empirical reconstruction down to oversampling ratios around 2.8 via spectral initialization + gradient descent, but no rigorous information-theoretic or algorithmic determination of the weak- and full-recovery thresholds $\alpha_{\mathrm{WR}}, \alpha_{\mathrm{FR}}$ for the FDF or $FD_1F\cdots D_\ell$ ensembles appears in the literature. The problem is listed among open problems in recent phase-retrieval surveys.

status_evidence.title: Structured Random Model for Fast and Robust Phase Retrieval
status_evidence.snippet: robust reconstruction is obtained at an oversampling ratio as low as 2.8
status_evidence.claim: Empirical results only; no rigorous threshold proofs for FDF / cascaded diffuser ensembles.

status_evidence.title: Phasebook: a survey of selected open problems in phase retrieval
status_evidence.snippet: survey of selected open problems in phase retrieval
status_evidence.claim: Recovery thresholds for structured measurement ensembles remain among the listed open problems.

status_evidence.title: Structured Random Models for Phase Retrieval with Optical Diffusers
status_evidence.snippet: cascade of structured transforms and random diagonal matrices
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to study these ensembles without resolving the threshold question.
